name: @prom.codes/context-mcp

tools.name: search_code
tools.description: PRIMARY code search for this workspace — the fast path to WHERE code lives. Hybrid retrieval (lexical FTS + dense vector over the actual source body + symbol-graph, RRF-fused, cross-encoder reranked) returns the top symbols AND an inline source snippet per hit — ONE call that replaces a manual Grep→Read loop, so prefer it for any code-location question. USE THIS FIRST when: you need a concept or behaviour ("where is auth handled?"), the exact symbol name is unknown or may have been renamed, the term is generic/high-frequency (grep would flood), or the repo is large or cross-language. Plain Grep is fine for an exact, known literal string in a known file — this tool wins on everything else, and returns the code inline so you usually don't need a follow-up read. Set `includeSnippet: false` for symbols only; `includeProvenance: true` adds the per-hit retrieval-channel scores (debugging/benchmarks).

tools.name: get_symbol
tools.description: Look up symbols by exact name. Optional `file` filters to one workspace-relative path.

tools.name: find_references
tools.description: All static references (calls / imports / member-access) whose target name matches.

tools.name: find_callers
tools.description: All symbols whose body calls the named symbol (inbound call-graph edge). Materialised from `call` / `member_access` references enclosed by the caller's byte-range.

tools.name: find_callees
tools.description: All symbols the named symbol calls (outbound call-graph edge). Resolves `call` / `member_access` references emitted from inside the symbol's body to their definitions.

tools.name: expand_context
tools.description: Symbol-graph expansion around a name. Returns neighbours bucketed by edge type (`defines` / `calls` / `imports` / `same-file`) and walk depth (1 = direct, 2 = neighbour-of-neighbour when `depth: 2`).

tools.name: get_file
tools.description: Read a UTF-8 file from the indexed workspace (resolved against the configured workspace root). Optional `startByte`/`endByte` slice; max 256 KiB.

tools.name: list_changed_since
tools.description: File records with `indexedAt > timestampMs`, ordered ascending. Use the largest returned `indexedAt` as the next cursor.

tools.name: list_workspaces
tools.description: Metadata for the workspace(s) this server knows about. Default `scope:"local"` returns the single composed workspace with its index roll-up (file/symbol/reference counts + per-language distribution). `scope:"cloud"` instead lists the tenant's SHARED-INDEX roster from the metered proxy — every repo in the cloud with its current snapshot summary (repo identity, git SHA, build age, size, file/symbol counts) — the "which repos are in the cloud" list (needs a PROMETHEUS_API_KEY).

tools.name: framework_overview
tools.description: High-level shape of the workspace: frameworks detected from manifest files (package.json, composer.json, requirements.txt, pyproject.toml) plus the per-language file distribution from the index. Heuristic and dependency-driven — absence of a hit means 'not declared in a manifest', not 'not used'.

tools.name: get_architecture
tools.description: One-call high-level map of the indexed workspace — the fast first move when onboarding onto an unfamiliar repo, replacing a dozen list/read calls. Returns: index size + embedding coverage, language mix, detected frameworks, packages/modules, top-level folder layout, symbol-kind breakdown, the most-referenced 'hotspot' symbols, and likely entry points. `hotspots` caps the hotspot list (`0` to skip it). NOTE: HTTP/route linking and community (Louvain) clustering are not extracted yet — see the `notes` field.

tools.name: index_status
tools.description: Health check for this workspace's code index. Reports the resolved workspace root, the on-disk index path, whether auto-indexing is enabled AND allowed for this root (it is refused for the home directory / filesystem root), how much is indexed (files / symbols / references + per-language counts), the embedding provider, and — best-effort, zero-cost — whether embeddings are reachable with the configured key. CALL THIS FIRST when `search_code` returns nothing, when you're unsure whether the right folder is indexed, or to confirm the API key works.

tools.name: reindex
tools.description: Manually rebuild this workspace's code index on demand: re-scan every file (parse + hash-diff; entries for files deleted on disk are removed), then run the embedding pass. COSTS MONEY: every symbol embedded is one metered embed call billed to the user's prom.codes quota — check `index_status.embeddings.pendingEmbed` FIRST to see the price, and do not call this speculatively or in a loop. By default the embed pass is INCREMENTAL — it embeds only new/changed symbols that are missing a vector (usually cheap), so call this to populate embeddings after fixing an API key or to pick up changes without restarting. `force: true` clears the snapshot and re-embeds EVERY symbol from scratch — that bills for the WHOLE repo, so only use it after switching embedding providers or to repair a corrupt snapshot, and tell the user what it will cost before you do. Requires a PROMETHEUS_API_KEY and a real project folder (refused for the home directory / filesystem root).

tools.name: pull_index
tools.description: Download this repo's SHARED team index snapshot (Premium/Team tier) and swap it into a local shared DB — so you inherit the team's fully-embedded index without re-embedding the shared code. Plug-and-play: with just a PROMETHEUS_API_KEY set, the repo identity is derived automatically from the git remote — no workspace id, no team-admin handoff. (Override with `repo`, or select an explicit server workspace UUID via `workspaceId` / PROMETHEUS_SHARED_WORKSPACE_ID.) Verifies checksum + embedding-space compatibility before swapping: it NEVER mixes embedding spaces and refuses on mismatch, so it can't corrupt a local index. The snapshot lands at ~/.prometheus/shared/<identity>.db and is used automatically on the next server start (auto-pull on boot is on by default). Safe to re-run: call it again to refresh when the team publishes a newer snapshot.

tools.name: install_hooks
tools.description: Make agents actually USE the prom.codes MCP tools by installing Claude Code 'active awareness' hooks. Server instructions + the CLAUDE.md rule are PASSIVE (the agent must remember to act); these hooks fire at the decision point: a SessionStart hook injects a binding directive (call memory_read; use search_code before grep) at turn 0 and after every compaction, and a UserPromptSubmit hook re-asserts it per prompt. A Stop hook additionally watches how full the context window is and raises the CONTEXT-HANDOVER trigger: at ~40% of the window the user is told a handover is coming up and the agent asks on the next prompt; at ~50% the agent actively proposes writing a handover file and continuing in a fresh session. It never forces or aborts anything — the user decides. Tune with PROMETHEUS_HANDOVER_NOTICE_TOKENS / _SUGGEST_TOKENS / _SHARE, PROMETHEUS_CONTEXT_WINDOW, or switch it off with PROMETHEUS_HANDOVER_HINT=off (PROMETHEUS_HANDOVER_INTERRUPT=off keeps the user-facing notice but never spends an extra turn). Writes a cross-platform Node hook to ~/.prometheus/hooks/ and adds a marked, REVERSIBLE entry to settings.json (backs the file up first; preserves any other hooks). `scope`: 'user' (default for this tool — ~/.claude/settings.json, applies to every project/window), 'project' (committed .claude/settings.json), or 'project-local' (gitignored .claude/settings.local.json — the auto-bootstrap target). `strict: true` ALSO installs an opt-in PreToolUse hook that denies Grep/Glob and redirects to search_code (stronger, but blocks legitimate non-code greps — off by default). `uninstall: true` removes the hooks we own. After install, the user must RELOAD their Claude Code window(s). Claude-Code-specific (Cursor / VS Code extension do not run hooks).

tools.name: dashboard
tools.description: Render the prom.codes LOCAL status dashboard as one self-contained HTML page and return its file path. It answers 'where do we stand?' across ALL sessions on this machine: which prom servers (context/memory/saver) are running where and in which version (heartbeats), whether npm updates are available, every locally indexed workspace with files/symbols and EMBEDDING COVERAGE %, memory-store totals, setup health (awareness hooks + a zero-cost API-key probe), and the current month's metered cloud usage. Read-only and local-first — only the cloud-usage tile queries the metered proxy. Pass `open: true` to also launch the page in the default browser; otherwise give the user the returned `htmlPath` to open.

tools.name: update_servers
tools.description: Safely update all three prom.codes servers (@prom.codes/context-mcp, memory-mcp, saver) to the latest npm versions. NEVER installs in-process (running servers lock their native modules on Windows — in-place npm install is the known EBUSY half-install trap). Instead it: (1) reports installed vs latest versions, the install kind (global/npx/dev), npm ignore-scripts hardening, and every prom server currently running (via heartbeats); (2) launches a DETACHED updater that waits until this session's server exits (user reloads/closes the windows), waits for — or with `force: true` terminates — the remaining servers, then runs the one documented upgrade command; (3) the result appears in `index_status.update.lastResult` after the restart. `dryRun: true` only reports the plan. `force: true` is explicit and never the default — it hard-terminates sibling servers (safe since 0.9.2: WAL is crash-consistent), use it when the user cannot close the other windows. ALWAYS tell the user exactly what to do next from the returned `nextSteps`.

instructions: This workspace is indexed by the prom.codes context engine. PREFER these tools over a manual grep/read loop when navigating code: search_code (hybrid semantic + lexical + symbol-graph — your FIRST move for any 'where/how is X' question, returns the code inline), get_symbol, find_references, find_callers, find_callees, expand_context, get_file. They are faster and more precise than scanning files by hand, especially on a large or unfamiliar repo. If search_code returns nothing or looks degraded, call index_status to check the index and the embedding key. If the user wants agents to reliably reach for these tools (and the memory tools) by default, call install_hooks to add Claude Code session hooks that enforce it. When the user asks where things stand (running servers, versions/updates, index & embedding coverage, memory, usage), call the dashboard tool — it renders a local HTML status page and returns its path.
